hmmt-feb-2004-geo-01.title: Cut off two right triangles
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-01.body:
Drop perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$ to $AD$, with feet $X$ and $Y$. Triangles $ABX$ and $DCY$ are $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ with hypotenuse $6$, so $BX=CY=3\sqrt2$ and each has area $\frac12(3\sqrt2)^2=9$.

The rectangle $BCYX$ therefore has area $30-18=12$ and height $3\sqrt2$, so $BC=\frac{12}{3\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-01.title: Area formula
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-01.body:
Let $BC=b$. The legs project $3\sqrt2$ each onto $AD$, so $AD=b+6\sqrt2$ and the height is $3\sqrt2$. Area $=\frac12(b+b+6\sqrt2)\cdot3\sqrt2=3\sqrt2\,(b+3\sqrt2)=30$, so $b+3\sqrt2=\frac{10}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2$, giving $b=2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-03.title: Two pools make a cylinder
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-03.body:
Turn a second copy of the pool upside down and fit it against the first: the depths add to $3+15=18$ at every point, so together they form a cylinder of height $18$ ft and radius $30$ ft with volume $\pi\cdot30^2\cdot18=16200\pi$. The pool is half of that: $8100\pi$ ft$^3$.

**Answer: $8100\pi$ ft$^3$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-03.title: Average depth
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-03.body:
The depth is linear in the east-west coordinate and the circle is symmetric about its centre, so the volume is (area) $\times$ (depth at the centre) $=\pi\cdot30^2\cdot\frac{3+15}{2}=900\pi\cdot9=8100\pi$.

**Answer: $8100\pi$ ft$^3$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-04.title: British flag theorem
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-04.body:
Let $P$ be at distance $w$ from side $AD$, $x$ from side $BC$, $y$ from side $AB$ and $z$ from side $CD$. By the Pythagorean theorem,
$$PA^2=w^2+y^2,\quad PB^2=x^2+y^2,\quad PC^2=x^2+z^2,\quad PD^2=w^2+z^2.$$
Hence $PA^2+PC^2=PB^2+PD^2$, so $PD^2=4+100-9=95$ and $PD=\sqrt{95}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{95}$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-05.title: Six sectors
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-05.body:
Split the plane into six sectors according to the signs of $x$, $y$, $x+y$. In each the inequality is linear:
- $x,y\ge0$: $2(x+y)\le1$, i.e. $x+y\le\frac12$.
- $x\ge0\ge y$, $x+y\ge0$: $x\le\frac12$. Similarly $y\le\frac12$ when $y\ge0\ge x$, $x+y\ge0$.
- $x\ge0\ge y$, $x+y\le0$: $y\ge-\frac12$. Similarly $x\ge-\frac12$ when $y\ge0\ge x$, $x+y\le0$.
- $x,y\le0$: $x+y\ge-\frac12$.

The region is a hexagon; in each sector it is an isosceles right triangle with legs $\frac12$ and area $\frac18$. Total area $6\cdot\frac18=\frac34$.

**Answer: $\frac34$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-06.title: Complete a parallelogram
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-06.body:
Choose $F$ on $AD$ with $BCDF$ a parallelogram. Then $BF=CD=8$ and $DF=BC=7$, so $AF=17-7=10$. Triangle $ABF$ has sides $6,8,10$, a right triangle with the right angle at $B$.

Since $BF\parallel CD$, the angle at $E$ equals $\angle ABF=90^\circ$.

**Answer: $90^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-07.title: Similar triangles
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-07.body:
Triangles $ADP$ and $CBP$ are similar (as $AD\parallel BC$) with area ratio $\frac12$, so their similarity ratio is $\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $PA:PC=PD:PB=1:\sqrt2$.

Scale so $[ADP]=1$. Triangles $ABP$ and $ADP$ share the vertex $A$ and have bases $BP$, $DP$ on one line with $BP=\sqrt2\,DP$, so $[ABP]=\sqrt2$; likewise $[CDP]=\sqrt2$. Also $[BCP]=2$. So $[ABCD]=1+2+\sqrt2+\sqrt2=3+2\sqrt2$.

$\frac{[ADP]}{[ABCD]}=\frac1{3+2\sqrt2}=3-2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3-2\sqrt2$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-08.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-08.body:
The triangle is similar to $3$-$4$-$5$, so it is right-angled. Put the right angle at $(0,0)$ and the other vertices at $(24,0)$ and $(0,18)$.
- Circumcentre: midpoint of the hypotenuse, $(12,9)$.
- Centroid: $\frac13(0+24+0,\,0+0+18)=(8,6)$.
- Inradius: $r=\frac{\text{Area}}{s}=\frac{216}{36}=6$, so the incentre is $(6,6)$.

The triangle with vertices $(6,6)$, $(8,6)$, $(12,9)$ has base $2$ (on $y=6$) and height $3$, so area $\frac12\cdot2\cdot3=3$.

**Answer: 3**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-09.title: Cut off four corners
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-09.body:
Place tetrahedron $ABCD$ with $A$ on top. The centre is $\frac34$ of the way from $A$ down to face $BCD$, so the reflection of face $BCD$ lies in a horizontal plane halfway between $A$ and $BCD$. It cuts off from $ABCD$ the small tetrahedron at $A$ obtained by scaling by $\frac12$ about $A$. Likewise the reflections of the other three faces cut off copies scaled by $\frac12$ about $B$, $C$, $D$.

The octahedron left over is mapped to itself by the reflection through the centre, so it lies in both tetrahedra; and everything removed lies outside the reflected tetrahedron. So the intersection is this octahedron, of volume
$$1-4\cdot\left(\tfrac12\right)^3=\tfrac12.$$

**Answer: $\frac12$**

hmmt-feb-2004-geo-10.title: Sine area formula
hmmt-feb-2004-geo-10.body:
The three angles at $Y$ are each $30^\circ$. Using $\text{area}=\frac12ab\sin30^\circ=\frac14ab$, the triangles $XYP$, $PYQ$, $QYZ$ have areas $\frac{XY\cdot PY}4$, $\frac{PY\cdot QY}4$, $\frac{QY\cdot YZ}4$. Their sum is the area of $XYZ$, namely $\frac12\cdot228\cdot2004=228456$.

Multiplying by $4$: $XY\cdot PY+PY\cdot QY+QY\cdot YZ=4\cdot228456$. Now expand
$$(PY+YZ)(QY+XY)=PY\cdot QY+PY\cdot XY+YZ\cdot QY+YZ\cdot XY=4\cdot228456+228\cdot2004=4\cdot228456+2\cdot228456=6\cdot228456=1370736.$$

**Answer: 1370736**
